subject: Regional cloud surge: diversion guidance for US/EU/APAC
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Acme Platform <ops@acme-platform.com>, Chris Holden <chris.holden@acme-platform.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Oct 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional cloud surge: diversion guidance for US/EU/APAC

Hi Chris / Maria —

Quick update: we observed a widespread peering/egress surge affecting a subset of instances in three provider regions (US-west, EU-central, APAC-southeast). Impact started ~08:50 PDT and resulted in intermittent elevated latencies and 502/504 errors for traffic routed through the affected zones.

What we’ve done so far (short):
- Automatically triggered regional fallback for affected hosts; most traffic has been rerouted to healthy zones.
- Opened an incident with the cloud provider (ticket INF-4321).
- Enabled sidecar routing and temporarily lowered our routing TTLs to 30s to speed client convergence.

Immediate actions we recommend on your side (Acme Platform) to minimize user impact:
1) If you control DNS for endpoints: reduce DNS TTL to 30s for the next 2–4 hours and monitor for convergence.
2) If you use region-pref endpoints: switch preference to the alternate region (instructions below).
   - US customers: prefer US-east-1 or US-central fallback endpoints (endpoint-reco.us.redwood.ai).
   - EU customers: switch to eu-west region endpoints (endpoint-reco.eu.redwood.ai).
   - APAC customers: prefer apac-central or apac-west fallback endpoints (endpoint-reco.apac.redwood.ai).
3) If you rely on a fixed IP/peering relationship, please confirm whether you have an alternate advertised path; if not, enable our sidecar routing as documented in the attached checklist.

We’re attaching a short checklist that walks through the exact steps your infra team can take right now (reroute-checklist.pdf). Ben and Priyom are standing by to coordinate the change window. If you want, we can run a short call to walk through step 2.

Estimated remediation window: we expect client-visible recovery within 30–90 minutes as routing converges; provider is investigating root cause. I’ll follow up with a post-incident note once we have the timeline and recommended durable mitigations.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: reroute-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme-platform.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Chris Holden <chris.holden@acme-platform.com>
Cc: ops@acme-platform.com
Date: Wed, 23 Oct 2029 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional cloud surge: diversion guidance for US/EU/APAC

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the quick heads-up. We are seeing elevated error rates in our EU and APAC tenants (~15% error rate for some endpoints) and some timeouts in our ingestion pipeline.

Two quick Qs:
- Can you confirm whether requests queued during the failover will be retried automatically or if we need to implement client-side retry/backoff?
- What SLA buffer should we expect for requests that hit the affected regions (for our incident reporting)?

We can do a quick 20-minute call in 15 if you’re free. Otherwise, please send the short run-through and we’ll implement the DNS TTL change immediately.

— Maria
Site Reliability Lead, Acme Platform
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Oct 2029 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional cloud surge: diversion guidance for US/EU/APAC

Vanessa — quick internal update for the thread so external recipients get a clear single response:
- We’ve enabled "bridge mode" on the affected clusters and spun up cross-region capacity; metrics show egress latency dropping back towards baseline within the last 6m for US-east fallback pool.
- Auto-retry behavior: our hosted SDK will retry idempotent requests up to 2x with exponential backoff; non-idempotent requests are not retried automatically. Recommend Acme enable client-side 429/5xx backoff for non-idempotent flows.
- SLA/metrics: note the provider outage qualifies as a third-party network event; we’ll treat impacted tokens as mitigated for usage-based credits per our SLA — we’ll review usage and apply adjustments where appropriate.

Action items I’m taking now:
1) Priyom and I will join the customer call and walk through the attached checklist and sidecar enablement.
2) Laura, please prepare a short post-incident summary and include a recommended TTL schedule and DNS records to publish.

I’ll draft a customer-facing one-pager and send here in the next 20m.

— Ben
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Acme Platform <ops@acme-platform.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme-platform.com>, Chris Holden <chris.holden@acme-platform.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Oct 2029 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — regional egress surge (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Maria / Chris —

Thanks again for your patience yesterday. Below is a short post-incident summary plus recommended next steps. I’ve attached the timeline CSV for your records (incident-timeline.csv) and included links to our internal postmortem and the provider ticket.

What happened (high level):
- At ~08:50 PDT on 2029-10-23, a provider-side peering disruption caused asymmetric egress latency spikes in specific availability zones across US-west, EU-central and APAC-southeast. The disruption manifested as elevated tail latency and increased 502/504 responses for traffic that transited the impacted egress paths.

Immediate mitigations performed by Redwood: 
- Enabled cross-region bridge mode and transient capacity scale-up (09:00 PDT).
- Decreased routing TTL to 30s and pushed a sidecar routing configuration to accelerate client convergence (09:05 PDT).
- Engaged provider support and opened INF-4321 (09:10 PDT).
- Monitored request-level retries and applied temporary rate smoothing for bursty tenants.

Customer-facing impact and refunds:
- Some requests in the affected regions experienced increased latency or transient errors during the 09:00–10:20 PDT window.
- Per our SLA, we will review billed usage and apply credits for requests that clearly failed as a result of the provider event. Ben will follow up with the usage window and proposed credit amounts.

Recommended durable actions (for Acme):
- Short term (now): set DNS TTL=30s for 2–4 hours to allow rapid failover during any residual instability.
- Mid term: enable our sidecar routing and configure region-preference failover. We can help run a dry-run during a low-traffic window.
- Long term: consider reserving Dedicated capacity in your highest-volume region (reduces reliance on shared egress paths).

Attached: reroute-checklist.pdf (step-by-step), incident-timeline.csv (event log).
Links: postmortem: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-postmortem-redwood-acme, ticket: https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/INF-4321

Next steps we’ll own:
- Ben will send the detailed usage window and credit proposal by EOD tomorrow.
- Laura will publish a sanitized postmortem to the shared drive and notify stakeholder distribution lists.
- Priyom will schedule a 30m runbook walk-through with Acme ops (please share the best time windows).

If you want us to run the DNS change together, Ben and Priyom are available for a quick window today.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll incorporate the root cause and provider remediation into our longer-term vendor reliability program.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
